claims.claim: Max-Bounded-Sums is linearly equivalent to selecting the largest offset whose contiguous equal-offset prefix-array mixed differences all meet the threshold.
claims.evidence: For P(i,j)=sum_{r<=i,c<=j} A(r,c), inclusion-exclusion makes each offset-l mixed difference exactly the corresponding l-square sum. Conversely, mixed differentiation of any integer P with zero top and left boundaries produces A, and double telescoping recovers P. Both transformations use O(mn) arithmetic/word operations.
claims.search_method: Re-derived both transforms algebraically and exhaustively checked signed matrices through 3 by 3.

claims.claim: An alleged optimum has a linear-time verifiable certificate, even for arbitrary signed entries.
claims.evidence: Scanning every L-square proves L feasible, and one violating square for every l>L proves no larger length feasible. Prefix sums make each check constant-time, giving O(mn+q)=O(mn) arithmetic/word operations. No monotonicity or sign restriction is used.
claims.witness: The certificate is the list {(l,i_l,j_l): l=L+1,...,q} with each indicated l-square sum greater than k; the verifier independently scans all L-squares.
claims.search_method: Checked the logical iff conditions and exhaustively verified certificates for small signed matrices and thresholds.

claims.claim: There is an exact output-sensitive search algorithm whose worst-case time is O(mn min(m,n)).
claims.evidence: Descending exhaustive search returns the greatest feasible length without assuming cross-length monotonicity. For m>=n=q and d=q-L, length n-t has (m-n+t+1)(t+1) placements. Summing through t=d yields O(mn+(m-n+1)(d+1)^2+(d+1)^3), which is O(mnq).
claims.witness: The first fully scanned length without a violation is L; every previously scanned length has a retained violating placement.
claims.search_method: Derived the placement sum and exhaustively compared the algorithm with brute-force optima on small signed matrices.

claims.claim: Positive-length feasibility has no universal cross-length structure: every Boolean pattern is realizable with O(log q)-bit signed entries.
claims.evidence: For any selected set T, the slot-r gadget has total 4 and makes length r infeasible. A smaller square wholly inside it contains at most one corner and has sum at most 1. Every other square contains a -H entry and has sum at most 4q-H=-4. Thus infeasible lengths are exactly T. Dimensions and threshold are common to all T, and H=4q+4 has O(log q) bits.
claims.witness: Use threshold 3, background -H, and in each selected r-slot place either the value 4 for r=1 or four unit-valued corners of an otherwise zero r-square.
claims.search_method: Proved the exhaustive inside-gadget/outside-gadget case split and checked every subset T through q=8 exactly.

claims.claim: Every deterministic algorithm that accesses an instance only through adaptive side-feasibility queries requires q queries in the worst case.
claims.evidence: On an all-infeasible transcript, stopping before querying every side leaves some r unqueried. The all-infeasible vector and the vector with only r feasible agree on every query but have optima 0 and r. Claim 3 realizes both with common dimensions and threshold, so any correct deterministic oracle algorithm must make q queries on that transcript.
claims.witness: Choose any unqueried r and compare feasibility vectors 0^q and the unit vector e_r.
claims.search_method: Applied an indistinguishability adversary and enumerated the transcript pairs for q through 10.

claims.claim: The feasibility-oracle obstruction persists under randomization: bounded-error randomized algorithms require Omega(q) queries in the worst case.
claims.evidence: Under probability 1/2 on the all-infeasible vector and 1/(2q) on each singleton-feasible vector, a deterministic t-query tree can be granted success on all queried singletons. On the remaining common transcript, output 0 gives success at most 1/2+t/(2q); any positive output gives at most (t+1)/(2q). Hence t<q/3 cannot attain 2/3 distributional success, and Yao's principle gives the stated worst-case randomized lower bound.
claims.witness: The hard distribution consists of 0^q with mass 1/2 and each e_r with mass 1/(2q).
claims.search_method: Re-derived the Yao bound with adaptive transcripts and checked its exact rational arithmetic for all queried subsets through q=10.

claims.claim: Feasibility can alternate at every side length, and the natural no-revisit greedy extension is incorrect.
claims.evidence: With alternating 1,-1 entries in the first row and zeros elsewhere, F_l=0 for even l and F_l=1 for odd l, so feasibility at k=0 alternates. In the 2 by 3 counterexample, the two side-2 sums are 1 and 4 while F_1=2. A scan that reduces to side 1 after the second side-2 placement but does not revisit earlier positions misses the value 2 and can incorrectly return 1 rather than 0.
claims.witness: At k=1, A=[[2,1,1],[-3,1,1]] has F_2=4 and F_1=2, so no positive length is feasible.
claims.search_method: Calculated the families symbolically and checked the exact sums for alternating matrices through n=32.

claims.claim: The O(mn) endpoint is achievable for two nontrivial signed separable classes: multiplicative rank one and additive separability.
claims.evidence: For A_ij=u_i v_j, l-square sums are products of independent u- and v-window sums, whose maximum is among four endpoint products. For A_ij=u_i+v_j, the maximum is l(max X_l+max Y_l). Computing window extrema for every length costs O(q(m+n))<=2mn. The stated recognition identities are necessary and sufficient; evaluating all four pivot-based quotients also handles a negative pivot.
claims.witness: For nonzero pivot p=A_rc, pA_ij=A_ic A_rj and each candidate square sum is XY/p; for additive matrices, A_ij=A_i1+A_1j-A_11.
claims.search_method: Proved the extrema reductions and tested signed random instances, including an exact negative-pivot representation.

claims.claim: A thresholded max-plus-convolution scan embeds exactly into matrices supported on one row.
claims.evidence: For length B-t, a top-row window from s telescopes to p_{s+B-t}-p_s. When i=s and j=t-s are valid, this equals C+x_i+y_j. If either index is invalid, the H/-H padding makes the value negative, whereas every valid value is at least 1. Squares below the supported row sum to zero, so F_{B-t}=C+c_t exactly. Since B-t decreases with t, the greatest feasible encoded length corresponds to the least coefficient satisfying c_t<=K.
claims.witness: The valid endpoints p_i=-x_i and p_{B-j}=y_j+C produce p_{B-j}-p_i=C+x_i+y_j.
claims.search_method: Checked every pair of vectors of length at most 3 over {-2,-1,0,1,2}, plus signed length-4 edge cases and arbitrary central prefix values.

claims.claim: If integer bit lengths are unbounded and bit operations are charged, an O(mn) bound independent of bit length is impossible.
claims.evidence: In an explicit-binary bit-access model, take a=k=2^(B-1) on a 1 by 1 instance. For every uninspected lower bit r, replacing a by a+2^r preserves the B-bit length and every other bit but changes the answer. Thus the equality execution must inspect all B-1 lower positions, giving Omega(B) bit cost. This does not imply a bounded-word or unit-cost lower bound.
claims.witness: The equality instance returns side 1, whereas each a=2^(B-1)+2^r with unchanged k returns 0.
claims.search_method: Applied a bit-probe indistinguishability argument and checked all alternative bits for B=2 through 128.

target_evidence: The source target requires either a general O(mn)-time algorithm for arbitrary signed integer matrices or an impossibility result at the corresponding substantive direct-access endpoint. The draft explicitly supplies neither. Its general algorithm is O(mn min(m,n)); the lower bounds apply only to side-feasibility oracle access; the O(mn) algorithms cover promised separable classes; the dense max-plus embedding gives no stronger lower bound; and the bit-cost argument is only an unbounded-input-length obstruction. These are correct, material partial results, and the parent's PARTIAL resolution claim is accurate.
